sources: SUNDAY Oct 18 2026 RUN (markets closed all weekend; every market field is the Friday Oct 16 US close or the last available tick). HEADLINE: NO NEW MARKET DATA SINCE FRIDAY, BUT FRED POSTED ITS OCT 16 OFFICIAL READINGS AND THEY SOFTEN THE EDGES OF YESTERDAY'S STAGFLATIONARY READ - AND THE FED-HIKE PANIC IN THE LAST RUN WAS OVERSTATED. FOUR CORRECTIONS VS THE OCT 17 RUN, ALL FROM OFFICIAL PRINTS THAT LANDED AFTER IT: (1) CURVE 0.33 -> 0.35. FRED T10Y2Y now carries Oct 16 at 0.35, versus the Oct 15 value of 0.33 the last run used as the latest. Sequence: 0.35 (Oct 16), 0.33 (Oct 15), 0.37 (Oct 14), 0.42 (Oct 13), 0.44 (Oct 9). So the week's flattening is 9bp, not 11bp, and the curve STEEPENED 2bp on the Oct 16 risk-off session rather than flattening further. Still the flattest stretch of this episode, still trending down, but the final session of the week went the other way. (2) BREAKEVENS 2.31 -> 2.33. FRED T5YIFR Oct 16 is 2.33, up from 2.31 (Oct 15), 2.34 (Oct 14), 2.33 (Oct 13), 2.32 (Oct 9). The 'new low' the last run flagged at 2.31 was a one-day dip, and 5y5y is now essentially unchanged on the week - trend revised from down to FLAT. The substance of the point survives and is arguably cleaner: realised CPI accelerated to 3.7 pct with a live 110 dollar oil shock, and long-run market-implied inflation did not move at all. That is anchored expectations, not a regime change. This remains the single most important tile on the board. (3) HY OAS 325 -> 323. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 Oct 15 is 3.23 pct, which supersedes the Oct 14 3.25 pct the last run used. Sequence: 3.23 (Oct 15), 3.25 (Oct 14), 3.16 (Oct 13), 3.11 (Oct 12), 3.11 (Oct 9). Credit has still broken decisively out of the 303-312 band to the wide side and is up 12bp on the week, but 323 is 2bp tighter than reported, not a fresh wide. The Oct 16 equity rout still post-dates this print, so the next reading is the one that matters. (4) MOVE 102.49 -> 101.10. Investing.com now serves an Oct 16 close of 101.10, versus 102.49 (Oct 15), 99.06 (Oct 14), 101.09 (Oct 13), 98.47 (Oct 9), 100.70 (Oct 8). Bond vol is up about 3 points on the week and still elevated, but it FELL 1.4 points on the Oct 16 session - the day equity vol spiked 30 pct. Equity vol and bond vol diverging on the same session is worth watching: it says Friday was an equity and credit event, not a rates event. THE BIG REVISION - FED ODDS WERE WRONG: the Oct 17 run reported roughly 50/50 odds of a hike at the Oct 27-28 FOMC, sourced to a Capital Economics comment. Prediction markets and futures disagree sharply and consistently: Kalshi 86.5-87 pct hold versus 12-13.5 pct hike, Polymarket 86.5 pct hold versus 13.5 pct hike, fed funds futures 84 pct hold versus 16 pct hike (all as of Oct 17). October hike odds last closed above 50 pct on Aug 18. So the market puts a hike at roughly ONE IN SEVEN, not a coin flip. This materially changes the read: the 'Fed tightens into an oil shock' policy-error scenario is a tail risk the market is largely dismissing, not the base case. Last run's framing overstated it. OIL - UNCHANGED AND STILL THE DRIVER: Brent 109.86 USD/Bbl, the Friday Oct 16 settle, plus 3.94 USD (3.72 pct) on the day and plus 4.9 pct on the week - the highest settlement since May 19, with a 110 intraday touch (TradingEconomics, FinanceFeeds). The supply story got more specific over the weekend: a missile aimed at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu export port was intercepted, a Ukrainian drone strike shut a main unit at a large Russian refinery, US commercial crude stocks fell 8.6 million barrels in the week to Oct 9 (largest draw since February), and Hormuz flows are running about 11.62 mb/d against a 17.15 mb/d baseline. IEA members agreed to release over 20 million barrels of diesel and the DOE requested proposals to exchange up to 17 million barrels of SPR crude; the sell-side read is that both are too small to close the gap. Week-ahead levels quoted: bull 115, base 105-112, bear 100. Trend up. EQUITY VOL - CARRIED, STILL UNCONFIRMED BY FRED: VIX 21.41 for Oct 16, up 4.97 points on the session and the highest in more than four months (Bloomingbit, Seeking Alpha, BigGo, miscw). FRED VIXCLS STILL has not posted an Oct 16 close - its latest remains 16.46 (Oct 15), with 16.87 (Oct 14), 15.27 (Oct 13), 15.21 (Oct 12), 14.84 (Oct 9). So the 21.41 figure is now in its third run as a wire-sourced value with no official confirmation, and the Oct 16 discrepancy flagged last run (21.41 wires versus 19.99 from the old GitHub Action) is STILL OPEN. Multiple independent outlets carry 21.41 with an explicit plus 4.97 delta off the 16.46 Oct 15 close, and one wrap cites 'the VIX hits 22', so the value is well corroborated even if unofficial. Versus 14.84 a week ago that is plus 6.57 points, about plus 44 pct. Trend up. FRED should settle this on Monday. DOLLAR - MARGINAL REVISION: DXY 101.837 for Oct 16, down 0.716 (0.70 pct) on the day (TradingEconomics). The same page also serves 101.7815 / minus 0.75 pct for the identical date; the last run used 101.78, this run uses 101.84. The 6bp difference is noise and does not change the read: a dollar that FALLS on a hawkish CPI surprise is still the odd one out on this board, and fits the AI-rout-plus-oil-shock story pressuring US assets better than a rates story. Versus 102.01 a week ago. Trend down. UNCHANGED TILES - NO NEW PRINTS SINCE FRIDAY: labour remains the strongest tile, initial claims 199k for the week ending Oct 10 (FRED ICSA, next release Oct 22), a fourth straight week below 200k after 198k (Oct 3), 199k (Sep 26), 198k (Sep 19), 198k (Sep 12); marginally higher on the week so trend up, but that is noise inside a historically tight range and firms are still not firing. NFCI minus 0.499 for the week ending Oct 9 (FRED, next release Oct 21), a fifth consecutive week of tightening from a very loose base - drift, not stress, and it pre-dates the Oct 16 selloff; the Oct 21 print is the first read that will include it. Trend up (tightening). Growth proxy 1.57 (copper 6.53 USD/Lbs plus 0.30 pct, gold 4,166.39 USD/t.oz minus 0.11 pct, both TradingEconomics Oct 16; 6.53/4166.39*1000 = 1.567) - third consecutive run identical at the second decimal. Trend flat. Consumer sentiment 46.3 (UMich preliminary October, from 48.1 final September), a five-month low with one-year inflation expectations at 4.7 pct and five-year at 3.5 pct, both UP - the uncomfortable combination with a 34 pct y/y gasoline move. Trend down. Real-economy tiles all carried with no new data: ISM Manufacturing 54.5 (September, next Nov 2), Sahm Rule 0.00 (September, next Nov 6, trigger is plus 0.50 so this is direction not signal), building permits 1,403k (August; September release lands Oct 20, two days out), LEI y/y minus 0.7 pct (September release Oct 22). All flat. MONETARY PLUMBING - STILL BLIND, THIRD RUN RUNNING: Fed funds target 3.75-4.00 pct after the September hike. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread was searched again and remains unavailable from any free source, so 0bp is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION, as is the EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis at minus 10bp. Global liquidity 1 (stable) - the Fed is hiking but no balance-sheet regime change was found; this tile is a judgement call, not a measurement. Two assumed tiles and one judgement tile out of eighteen. INFRASTRUCTURE - CLEAN RUN, TWO ITEMS STILL OPEN: git is healthy, the working tree was clean at start, and the duplicate-writer problem the last run flagged is RESOLVED - the GitHub Action was disabled on Oct 17 and this scheduled session is now the sole writer of data.json. The BDTI tile was removed from the dashboard on Oct 17 after nineteen runs of non-informative carried data; it is gone from this payload. STILL OPEN AND UNRESOLVED FOR A THIRD RUN - SECURITY: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token embedded in plain text in .git/config. The task description says it is a fine-grained token scoped to this repo, which limits the blast radius, but a plaintext PAT on disk should still be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. ALSO STILL PRESENT: untracked junk in the repo root from earlier workarounds - _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/ - all safe to delete. PICTURE: a weekend run with no new market data is normally a formality, but this one matters because the official Oct 16 prints revise four tiles and the Fed-odds correction revises the conclusion. The direction of travel from last week is intact and still bad: inflation re-accelerated to 3.7 pct and beat consensus, oil added a 4.9 pct supply-side shock straight into the next CPI print, credit broke out of its band to the wide side, the curve is at the flattest of this episode, equity vol is up 44 pct on the week and the consumer's inflation expectations rose while sentiment hit a five-month low. But three things now argue against the policy-error framing the last run adopted. The market prices a hike at one in seven, not one in two. Long-run breakevens did not fall to a new low - they are flat at 2.33, which is the market saying it still believes the Fed. And the curve steepened 2bp on the Friday rout while bond vol fell, which is what an equity and credit event looks like, not a rates event. Add claims below 200k for a fourth week and the honest read is: a live energy shock sitting on top of an AI-valuation and credit unwind, with the labour market and inflation expectations both still holding, and a Fed that the market expects to sit still. That is a risk-off configuration with a supply-side inflation problem attached - not yet a recession setup, and not the imminent policy error. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: the Oct 27-28 FOMC, where the market now says hold at roughly 85 pct - a hike would be a genuine surprise and the single biggest repricing risk on the board; whether 5y5y breakevens hold 2.33 or start pricing a regime change; whether HY OAS keeps widening past 323 once the Oct 16 rout is in the data; whether VIX holds above 20 and whether FRED's Oct 16 close finally confirms 21.41 or lands nearer the Action's 19.99; whether 2s10s holds 35bp or inverts; whether claims break 200k on Oct 22; whether Brent holds above 105 (bull 115, bear 100) and the EIA report on Oct 21; September building permits Oct 20, NFCI Oct 21 for the first post-selloff read, September LEI Oct 22; rotating the embedded PAT.
